However, excessive noise levels can lead to stress, anxiety, and even contribute to the development of mental health disorders such as depression and hypertension. Chronic exposure to loud noises can cause fatigue, irritability, and sleep disturbances, which in turn can exacerbate mental health issues.

This is known as "sound deprivation" or "sonic hole," where the lack of expected auditory cues can lead to feelings of isolation and unease.

In summary, ambient noise plays a nuanced role in mental health. It can be beneficial in moderation, but excessive or insufficient noise can negatively impact our psychological well-being.
